subject: rstan with Linux vs. Windows: "type qualifier on return type is meaning" warning from Cpp

messages.author: fca42ed043bd3ff5
messages.subject: rstan with Linux vs. Windows: "type qualifier on return type is meaning" warning from Cpp
parts:
Dear all,
when looking at the type of warning below ("type qualifier on return type is meaningless"), what do you make of it and is it concerning? I managed to reproduce this warning for a basic 8 schools example (files attached), so I suspect that this is not due to how I wrote the model.

I am getting this on Linux using rstan_2.7.0-1 when compiling a model that resulted in no such warning when compiling it on Windows. Am I right in assuming that this warning means that the particular compiler dislikes how some of standard C++ code for rstan is auto-generated? And is it more a stylistic thing that the compiler dislikes or something that indicates that something is really wrong (the model does subsequently sample, but I wanted to understand what is up with this warning)?

I found the following suggested resolutions: remove the type qualifier from the return type of the function (not sure how I would control this, if this is relating to code that is automatically generated by rstan) or ignore this diagnostic warning (um, okay, if there is no real issue...).

Many thanks,
Björn

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] rstan with Linux vs. Windows: "type qualifier on return type is meaning" warning from Cpp
parts:
The warning says that when you return an object by value it’s
redundant to qualify the return type with “const” as you’ll never
get to modify it.  The const qualifiers should technically be
removed, but it will not affect the actual code and so they can
be safely ignored.  If you would be so kind, it would be great
if you could create an issue on this matter in the RStan
repository.
